support.quote: Er nimmt als größtes Landraubtier in Deutschland eine besondere Stelle im Ökosystem ein.

assessments.note: Official Bundestag server copy of the same Drucksache (s1 is a party-site mirror). Only 'land' makes it true: the grey seal (Kegelrobbe, up to 300 kg) is Germany's largest predator overall.

support.quote: das größte in Deutschland freilebend vorkommende Raubtier (bis zu 300 kg schwer und 2,5 Meter groß)

assessments.note: Premise check: the qualifier 'land' in the wording is needed, since the grey seal is the largest predator in Germany overall; the wolf is the largest on land.

support.quote: Growing genetic resistance in the remaining rabbits had allowed the population to recover to 200–300 millio

assessments.note: Australia alone holds some 200–300 million feral European rabbits, Europe and the farmed rabbits of China many more; no census of North American cottontails supports 'more than half of all rabbits'. The 'half' line also once stood in English Wikipedia's Rabbit article but has been removed. Kept only as a widely repeated claim (wording reframed).

support.quote: (This explains why almost half of the rabbit population lives in North America.)

assessments.note: Apparent origin of the trivia: an unsourced 1998 student page, later cited by Wikipedia. Confirms only that the claim exists and names North America (the wording is reframed as 'according to a widely repeated claim'); the population claim itself is unsupported.

support.quote: More than half the world's rabbit population resides in North America

assessments.note: Shows how the claim spread: Wikipedia carried it (citing the 1998 Texas Tech student page) until it was removed; the current article no longer says so. Confirms the claim's wording, not the population fact.
